Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh's bowlers were erratic in the first 25 overs but then picked themselves up to redeem their efforts a bit. The spinners were tidy and picked a couple wickets each while Mortaza too struck twice in his second spell as Bangladesh clawed their way back into the contest. The fielding though was mostly dismal with simple catches being put down right from the first over when Latham got a reprieve on 0. That proved costly but this target is gettable although the wicket isn't that flat. Join us shortly for the chase.

Excellent comeback by Bangladesh in the second half but this is still a good total by New Zealand. Skipper Latham and Broom conjured fifties as their 133-run stand provided a lovely platform for the Kiwis to launch to a massive total. However, that didn't quite happen as they slipped from a comfortable 156/1 to 226/7 in the space of 15 overs as Bangladesh pulled things back. However, veteran Taylor's unbeaten fifty ensured that New Zealand breached the 270-run mark.

TEAM CHANGES - New Zealand have made three changes, all in their bowling. HENRY, PATEL and BENNETT come in place of Kuggeleijn, Milne and Sodhi. Bangladesh have left out Sunzamul and NASIR comes in for him.

PITCH REPORT - It appears to be a decent batting surface although there should be some help for the bowlers early in the morning. There are quite a few patches on the track as well and there should be some grip for the spinners. A score of 290-300 is predicted to be a good score.
TOSS - BANGLADESH WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO FIELD.

Hello and welcome to the final game of the tri-series with New Zealand facing Bangladesh in Dublin. The trophy has already been sealed by the Kiwis and this game will be a platform for both sides to polish their Champions Trophy preparations. Conditions here are a bit conducive to the bowlers although batting isn't that difficult if you can dig in. It shall be interesting to see if both teams opt to rotate the squad. The toss isn't far away.
